Museum objects, ready for the browser

As a digital heritage intern at Flyover Zone, I turned photogrammetric datasets, point clouds and camera data into visualisation-ready 3D assets. The work is part of a Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum collection project.

  • 17 photogrammetric models optimised into production-ready .sog assets for web visualisation.
  • Gaussian splats created and refined in Agisoft Metashape, Brush and SuperSplat, for immersive 3D environments.

2025–26M.Sc. thesis
University of Padova with CNR-ISPC
Rome

A lost pavement, rebuilt with its evidence attached

For my thesis I reconstructed the pavement of the Basilica Julia in the Roman Forum. I registered Normand's 1852 drawing onto a photogrammetric model of the site, then modelled 266 marble slabs one by one in Blender.

Each slab is linked to its material, dimensions and source through a knowledge graph built with the Extended Matrix, so the model shows how sure we are about every piece.

How each slab is supported

Schematic. Tile positions are illustrative, not the real slab layout.

Bilkent University
Ankara

A Tanagra figurine, built digitally and printed at full scale

I built a scale-accurate model from reference imagery and artefact measurements in Agisoft Metashape and Fusion 360. I then prepared the mesh for a full-scale PLA print and used the print to check scale and proportion.

Ankara

Recording objects in a conservation unit

I photographed ceramic and sculptural artefacts and processed them in Agisoft Metashape, from image alignment through dense point cloud and mesh to texture. I also made technical drawings and material and damage maps in GIMP at 1:1 scale, working alongside the conservators.

Image acquisition → alignment → dense point cloud → mesh → texture
